architecture_principles: physical discovery comes before candidate ranking
the Agent uses measured rheological regularities as scientific tools rather than optimizing benchmark recovery
state-aware rheology, external chemistry evidence and process uncertainty serve distinct scientific roles
candidate selection should maximize usefulness and interpretability for the observed material failure mode
deterministic calculations are separated from language-model judgment
the Skeptic and Robustness Adjudicator are decision-quality controls, not components that need ablation to justify their existence
the final recommendation is frozen before physical adjudication
only concise auditable outputs are stored; hidden chain-of-thought is not scientific evidence
held-out result data are structurally removed before outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction payloads are assembled
external analogue percentages define supported regions, not exact local optima
performance mitigation and causal isolation are distinct experiment intents; single-factor attribution is not the universal default
among similarly supported candidates, the minimum sufficient intervention is preferred
architecture.canonical_flow: planner(intent + failure mode) -> evidence/tool layer -> proposer -> skeptic -> robustness adjudicator -> judge -> freeze
architecture.claim_boundary: V3.4.0 is an outcome-blind reconstruction of the preexperimental decision state using only evidence available before the validation result. It may support recovery of the scientific problem, intervention family, and formulation neighborhood, but it must not be described as a recovered contemporaneous machine record or as proof that the exact historical recipe was independently predicted.

evaluation_priority: physical wet-lab adjudication of the selected point
traceable use of measured local regularities

architecture.name: PUR_NEW_PREEXPERIMENTAL_RECONSTRUCTION_AGENT_V3
non_goals: proving that every internal Agent module is individually necessary through ablation
making architecture benchmarking the main scientific contribution
optimizing held-out-region recovery as the main objective
claiming that literature-prior proximity predicts the wet-lab outcome
replacing the material-science result with an LLM-systems paper
primary_agent_outputs: material regularities used in the decision
design implication derived from each regularity
measurement plan tied to the discovered failure mode
architecture.purpose: Outcome-blind scientific decision Agent that reconstructs the preexperimental decision state: it extracts material-response regularities from measured PUR rheology, selects an intervention strategy, and freezes one useful formulation-process experiment point without access to the later validation formulation or outcome.
required_scientific_sequence: state the positive material regularities and their boundaries
translate those regularities into a design objective
use external evidence to identify chemically plausible intervention directions
adjudicate robustness to reasonable alternative evidence interpretations
freeze one useful experiment point and a falsifiable measurement criterion
architecture.secondary_replay_role: Deprecated for the current study narrative. The active Stage-1 evaluation is a single outcome-blind preexperimental reconstruction, not an Arm A/Arm B replay comparison.

stages.role: identify the physical failure mode, upstream rheological regularities, evidence needs and measurement objective before candidate ranking
execute read-only scientific tools, including the paper-derived state-aware rheology tool, external evidence retrieval, formulation inspection and process-state audits
rank experiment points according to scientific usefulness for the discovered material problem
try to falsify the provisional recommendation and test scientific interpretability, leakage and claim boundaries
adjudicate whether the proposed point remains useful under alternative evidence priorities, process-state uncertainty and the skeptic's strongest objections
resolve proposer, skeptic and robustness records and make the final pre-result decision
programmatically validate and freeze the recommendation with timestamp, hashes, model, candidate state, uncertainty and falsifiable acceptance criterion

deterministic_decision_diagnostics.intervention_sufficiency_rule: Decision order is: failure mode -> experiment intent -> required intervention-axis coverage -> evidence-supported candidates -> minimum sufficient intervention. For performance_mitigation, candidates covering EVERY independently supported axis (acrylic_like, minor_tackifier_like) are compared first. Minimum sufficient intervention is a tie-break WITHIN that group only. A candidate that zeroes an independently supported axis is a partial-coverage / mechanistic control, not the default performance rank-1; it must not become rank-1 merely because zeroing that axis lowers modifier burden.
deterministic_decision_diagnostics.note: These are transparent decision diagnostics, not fitted property predictions. Exact literature-anchor distance is retained only for audit and is not a primary ranking objective. Performance-mitigation and causal-isolation scenarios are separated so that single-factor attribution is not the default for every experiment.

acceptance_criterion.claim: S1C41 mitigates the local 120 C hot-hold viscosity-drift failure under matched process and state-control conditions.
acceptance_criterion.criterion: Success requires SI15-60=(eta60-eta15)/eta15 <= 0.20 at 120 C, with the result supported by the 120 C 15 min state anchor and repeat or matched-reference/control review; if 90 min is collected, SI15-90 should be <= 0.35 as secondary support.
acceptance_criterion.failure_condition: Fail the mitigation claim if SI15-60 > 0.20, if drift is not materially below the E5 high-drift reference under matched controls, if only static viscosity improves, or if missing state/process controls make the comparison uninterpretable.
acceptance_criterion.measurement_window: 120 C hold, primary 15-60 min; secondary 15-90 min where available, with an 80-130 C temperature sweep as a secondary processability check.

alternatives_considered.relative_reason: Full-coverage and lower total modifier burden, but its 2.5 wt% TK100 is below the repeated 4.8-6.4 wt% tackifier-like cluster; for performance mitigation S1C41 provides stronger supported-axis coverage for only 2.5 wt% additional modifier.

Full-coverage with stronger acrylic-region alignment and 5 wt% TK100, but it increases total modifier burden to 22.5 wt% and departs further from the E2 local chemistry than needed for the first mitigation test.

Strong coarse analogue-region test at 20 wt% acrylic plus 5 wt% tackifier, but the 25 wt% total modifier burden is a larger first intervention and should not be selected solely for closeness to external priors.
Useful acrylic-only causal-isolation control, but it zeroes the independently supported minor_tackifier_like axis and therefore does not test the declared performance-mitigation strategy.
Baseline/no-intervention control; useful for reference but does not test the resin-modification mitigation hypothesis.

judge_normalized.selection_rationale: Select S1C41 as the frozen performance-mitigation experiment. Local experiments established the failure mode: 120 C hold data show low drift for E1 and high drift for E5, while E2 has large realization/process spread; therefore the next experiment must be judged by matched hold-window SI rather than static viscosity. Paper-derived rheological rules from the state-aware summary show monotonic Andrade-like temperature response over 80-130 C, separation of static viscosity from hold stability, and the need for a 120 C state anchor. Curated PUR literature/database priors support acrylic-like modification as a broad 15-25 wt% region and minor tackifier-like modification near 5 wt% with a conservative upper region below about 10 wt%; these guide the formulation family but are not treated as direct predictors of the candidate outcome. Conservative experimental-design constraints require full coverage of both independently supported axes for performance_mitigation, matched 120 C hold measurement, process-state control, and minimum sufficient modifier burden only after axis sufficiency is met. This resolves the Skeptic and Robustness objections by choosing S1C41 over S1C40: S1C40 is lower burden but its 2.5 wt% tackifier is a conservative low-dose probe below the strongest tackifier evidence, while S1C41 keeps the same 15 wt% acrylic level and moves TK100 to 5 wt% for a more robust full-coverage mitigation test. S1C46 and S1C51 are held as heavier robustness alternatives; S1C49 is reserved for causal isolation because it removes the supported tackifier axis. The decision does not rely on exact analogue distance or held-out wet-lab information.

extrapolation.note: S1C41 is outside the local measured modifier-free chemistry but inside the curated broad modifier-region priors; it is not an exact-property prediction.

action_requests.reason: Retrieve the measured low-drift original reference trajectory and SI descriptors for direct comparison to the intended hold-stability objective.

action_requests.name: get_hold_stability
action_requests.reason: Retrieve the measured high-drift original reference trajectory and SI descriptors to quantify the local failure mode that the next candidate should mitigate.

action_requests.name: get_repeatability_risk
action_requests.reason: E2 is the reactive-core anchor for the candidate lattice and has large run spread in the supplied data; its repeatability risk must be explicit before using nominal viscosity as a baseline.

action_requests.reason: Confirm the measured temperature support and choose any viscosity anchor temperature inside the supported 80-130 C range, avoiding unsupported extrapolation.

action_requests.reason: After defining the local design objective, retrieve the evidence-derived candidate-space hypothesis, including the E2 anchor, independent acrylic/tackifier axes, and claim boundary, before any candidate-specific ranking.

action_requests.reason: Collect source-level acrylic analogue evidence to distinguish directly commensurate numeric anchors from directional or noncommensurate evidence before bounding candidate acrylic levels.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Collect source-level tackifier analogue evidence and conservative upper-bound guidance for the minor tackifier axis without treating literature percentages as exact local optima.

action_requests.name: query_external_priors
action_requests.reason: Retrieve directional stability-support evidence for modifier-family effects on hot-hold viscosity rise, while preserving limitations from non-identical chemistry, MDI levels, and hold schedules.

candidate_evaluation_dimensions: Hot-hold stability at 120 C using SI=(eta_t1-eta_t0)/eta_t0 over the measured local windows, especially 15-60 min and 15-90 min if available.
Initial or early-hold viscosity level at a temperature inside measured support, without allowing this nominal value to dominate hold-drift mitigation.
Temperature-response shape over 80-130 C, including monotonicity and consistency with the local Andrade-like trend.
State-aware realization/process risk, including whether one-point calibration or replicated runs are needed to compare candidate and references.
Distance from the E2 reactive-core anchor in acrylic-like, tackifier-like, combined modifier, polyol, and MDI fractions.
Stoichiometric plausibility and unknown reactive-group/functionality effects, especially for acrylic-like modifiers with uncertain OH or other reactive functionality.
External-evidence category: directly commensurate numeric anchor, directional/noncommensurate analogue, or conservative design-bound principle.
Feasibility within the candidate lattice and within the claim boundary that no held-out validation formulation or outcome is used.
counterfactual_checks: Would a reactive-core-only E2-like candidate with state calibration explain the observed viscosity level without improving hold drift? If yes, nominal viscosity alone is not adequate evidence.

Would a single-axis acrylic-only candidate in the externally anchored 15-25 wt% region test the same mitigation hypothesis with less attribution ambiguity? Use this only if causal isolation becomes the priority.

Would a minor tackifier-only candidate address processability but leave the established hot-hold drift failure unresolved? If so, it is a weaker performance-mitigation choice unless supported by stability evidence.

Would a combined acrylic-plus-minor-tackifier candidate remain within independently supported bounded regions while reducing extrapolation from either axis alone? If yes, it is admissible for performance mitigation.

Would the apparent improvement disappear after applying one-point state calibration or comparing against E1/E5 hold references? If yes, the result should be attributed to process state or measurement variation rather than formulation performance.
Does any ranking rationale depend on the held-out validation formulation identity or later wet-lab outcome? If yes, reject that rationale under the blind pre-result evidence policy.
planner.decision_goal: Select one prospective candidate from the blinded candidate lattice only after confirming that the next experiment is aimed at reducing the locally observed hot-hold viscosity drift, not merely matching a nominal viscosity at one temperature.
design_implications: The next experiment should target reduced hot-hold drift within the local 120 C hold window while retaining measurable melt-processability inside the 80-130 C sweep range.

A multi-component modifier intervention is admissible because the intent is performance mitigation and both acrylic-like and tackifier-like axes have independent prior support, provided the selected point remains inside bounded evidence-supported regions.

Candidate ranking should penalize large extrapolation from the E2 reactive-core anchor, unknown stoichiometric/process-state effects, and any formulation that relies only on a nominal viscosity match without a hold-stability rationale.

Acrylic-like loading around the externally repeated 15-25 wt% analogue region can be considered a broad prior region, not an exact optimum; the 30 wt% lattice upper bound is a conservative search boundary rather than directly commensurate evidence.
Minor tackifier-like loading up to about 10 wt% is supported as a conservative bounded axis; directional tackifier evidence should not be converted into an exact total-formulation optimum.
Because local repeatability/state effects are large, the chosen candidate should include state-aware measurement or calibration, not only one unreplicated temperature sweep.
material_regularities_to_use: Measured temperature sweeps for original formulations are monotonic decreasing over 80-130 C and are well described locally by Andrade-like temperature dependence, so candidate assessment should stay inside measured temperature support unless new measurements justify extrapolation.

E2 shows large nominal run spread across temperature sweeps, with CV roughly 0.46-0.58 and max/min ratios around 2.8-3.6, so realization or process state must be treated as an explicit uncertainty dimension.

Original thermal-hold data at 120 C show a strong contrast: E1 has relatively low drift over the 15-60 and 15-90 min windows, while E5 has much larger positive drift, establishing hold stability as an independent response from initial viscosity.
The payload distinguishes viscosity level, temperature response, thermal-hold stability, and process-state/repeatability; these should not be collapsed into one scalar viscosity objective.

External PUR evidence supports acrylic-like and tackifier-like modifier families as chemically plausible intervention axes, but most anchors are analogues or directional stability contexts rather than direct local optima.
planner.physical_failure_mode: Thermal-hold viscosity drift during hot holding at 120 C is the primary demonstrated failure mode; nominal viscosity level and monotonic temperature response are secondary constraints, and realization/process-state spread prevents treating a single sweep viscosity as a complete material property.
required_measurements_for_adjudication: Thermal-hold trajectory at 120 C over the same local time support used for original references, including at least 15, 60, and preferably 90 min points to compute SI comparably.
Temperature sweep over 80-130 C for the chosen candidate, preserving source units and avoiding extrapolated viscosity claims.
At least one process-state or calibration measurement sufficient to place the candidate on the state-aware rheology structure if the master-curve summary indicates state calibration matters.
Repeat or replicate information sufficient to distinguish formulation effect from realization/process-state spread, especially if candidate viscosity differences are comparable to E2 run spread.
Transparent formulation composition audit including modifier fractions, combined modifier fraction, reactive-core fractions, and any stoichiometric assumptions.
uncertainty_triggers: If the state-aware rheology summary shows that state shifts dominate formulation-only prediction, candidate comparison must include state calibration before declaring performance improvement.
If the selected candidate lowers initial viscosity but has unchanged or larger SI drift, it should not be considered successful performance mitigation.
If measured candidate viscosity falls outside the original 80-130 C support or requires extrapolation to interpret, classify the inference as out-of-domain or only partially supported.
